data.reasoning: The package is a standard AppImage wrapper with fully checksummed sources from a GitHub repository. The PKGBUILD contains no malicious code, only standard extraction and compilation of a small SELinux compatibility shim. The disagreement was caused by a transient API error (HTTP 400) in the qwen model during the full PKGBUILD review, not by actual security concerns.
data.disagreement_analysis: The qwen model returned 'inconclusive' solely due to an LLM API failure (HTTP 400) when reviewing the PKGBUILD in the second pass. The deepseek model successfully reviewed all files and found them safe. Both models' successful analyses agree that the package is safe.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to complete the full PKGBUILD review due to an API error (HTTP 400).
learnings: Transient API errors during file review should trigger a retry rather than immediately failing the file and marking the package as inconclusive, especially when the initial parse and other files are safe.
Ensure models analyze the full PKGBUILD (including prepare/package functions) in the initial pass if possible, to avoid missing build-time risks if the second pass fails.
